data.current_description:
Return requested attributes for one place or a list of places. Standard attributes (opening_hours, phone, website, facebook, instagram, tiktok, email, existence, open_closed) cost one credit per place however many you request; any other attribute name is a research field, answered by a bounded research loop and charged per place per field. A request may mix both and pays for each. Send poi_name for one place and get the flat response; send pois for a list and get a rows-by-attributes matrix. include_summary=true also returns a short factual place_summary. Requires a key with the enrich or deep_research entitlement; either one may request any attribute, standard or custom. See [Research custom attributes](/docs/guides/research-custom-attributes/) for custom attributes.

### Verifying the name and address you sent

When your records may be close but not exact - an abbreviation, an initialism, a
store number, or a slightly stale spelling - three independent checks are
available, one for each thing a record can get wrong:

- `verify_name` settles what the business is actually called BEFORE researching
  anything else, and every attribute you asked for is then researched against
  the verified name. Each row carries `identity.name`.
- `verify_address` checks the trading address AFTER research and never replaces
  it. Each row carries `address_checks.address`.
- `verify_registered_address` checks the registered office. Each row carries
  `address_checks.registered_address`.

`identity.name` gives the value we settled on, a verdict, and your original. The
verdict is `confirmed` (yours was already right), `corrected` (we replaced it) or
`unresolved` (we could not establish it, so your value comes back untouched).
`value` is always what the rest of the row was researched against, so branch on
the verdict rather than comparing strings.

Formatting is not a correction: punctuation, casing, "and" vs "&" and a dropped
or added Inc/Ltd/LLC all come back `confirmed` with your own string.

`verify_name` and `verify_address` share one lookup, so either or both cost a flat
1 extra credit per row, independent of how many attributes you requested;
`verify_registered_address` costs 1 more. Each can be overridden per place.

`verify_identity` is deprecated. It means `verify_name` plus `verify_address`,
costs the same 1, and additionally rewrites the address research runs against to
the same premises written in full - never a different one - returning
`identity.address` too. Use the separate flags in new integrations, so a place can
decline either check on its own.

This is not a postal validation - a `confirmed` address matches what the business
publishes about itself, not a postal database - and it makes no claim about
whether the business is still open.


### Owner discovery (`owners`, `owner_org`)

`owners` is the individual owner, co-owners or franchisee, as one value: a list
of people with a `name` and a `role`. Add `include` (`phone`, `email`,
`linkedin`) to look up each owner's direct contacts, returned in the same
objects. `owner_org` is the operating company when no individual owner exists.
They are mutually exclusive per place: when one is established, the other
abstains. "no individual owner" is a legitimate answer. `key_people` takes the
same shape with `title` in place of `role`.

`owners` and `key_people` carry no confidence score. Unavailable ownership is a
normal result; do not interpret an abstention as a claim that no owner exists.
`owners` and `key_people` cost 1 credit for the names, 1 for the roles or
titles and 1 per included contact; `owner_org` is billed like any other field.
See [Owners and key people](/docs/guides/owners-and-key-people/).

The callee is on hold during the entire 60-second budget (POST + wait time). This operation updates the webhook configuration for the API key.

data.current_description:
Return requested attributes for one place or a list of places. Standard attributes (opening_hours, phone, website, facebook, instagram, tiktok, email, existence, open_closed) cost one credit per place however many you request; any other attribute name is a research field, answered by a bounded research loop and charged per place per field. A request may mix both and pays for each. Send poi_name for one place and get the flat response; send pois for a list and get a rows-by-attributes matrix. include_summary=true also returns a short factual place_summary. Requires a key with the enrich or deep_research entitlement; either one may request any attribute, standard or custom. See [Research custom attributes](/docs/guides/research-custom-attributes/) for custom attributes.

### Verifying the name and address you sent

When your records may be close but not exact - an abbreviation, an initialism, a
store number, or a slightly stale spelling - three independent checks are
available, one for each thing a record can get wrong:

- `verify_name` settles what the business is actually called BEFORE researching
  anything else, and every attribute you asked for is then researched against
  the verified name. Each row carries `identity.name`.
- `verify_address` checks the trading address AFTER research and never replaces
  it. Each row carries `address_checks.address`.
- `verify_registered_address` checks the registered office. Each row carries
  `address_checks.registered_address`.

`identity.name` gives the value we settled on, a verdict, and your original. The
verdict is `confirmed` (yours was already right), `corrected` (we replaced it) or
`unresolved` (we could not establish it, so your value comes back untouched).
`value` is always what the rest of the row was researched against, so branch on
the verdict rather than comparing strings.

Formatting is not a correction: punctuation, casing, "and" vs "&" and a dropped
or added Inc/Ltd/LLC all come back `confirmed` with your own string.

`verify_name` and `verify_address` share one lookup, so either or both cost a flat
1 extra credit per row, independent of how many attributes you requested;
`verify_registered_address` costs 1 more. Each can be overridden per place.

`verify_identity` is deprecated. It means `verify_name` plus `verify_address`,
costs the same 1, and additionally rewrites the address research runs against to
the same premises written in full - never a different one - returning
`identity.address` too. Use the separate flags in new integrations, so a place can
decline either check on its own.

This is not a postal validation - a `confirmed` address matches what the business
publishes about itself, not a postal database - and it makes no claim about
whether the business is still open.


### Owner discovery (`owners`, `owner_org`)

`owners` is the individual owner, co-owners or franchisee, as one value: a list
of people with a `name` and a `role`. Add `include` (`phone`, `email`,
`linkedin`) to look up each owner's direct contacts, returned in the same
objects. `owner_org` is the operating company when no individual owner exists.
They are mutually exclusive per place: when one is established, the other
abstains. "no individual owner" is a legitimate answer. `key_people` takes the
same shape with `title` in place of `role`.

`owners` and `key_people` carry no confidence score. Unavailable ownership is a
normal result; do not interpret an abstention as a claim that no owner exists.
`owners` and `key_people` cost 1 credit for the names, 1 for the roles or
titles and 1 per included contact; `owner_org` is billed like any other field.
See [Owners and key people](/docs/guides/owners-and-key-people/).
